messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx/timeouts observed for private-vpc egress -> gateway-proxy-1 (us-west-2). Error rate ~15% over last 5m. Pager: oncall-network paged.

alice.m: I'm on it (oncall-network). Can someone confirm impacted tenants and customer-facing scope?

ben_t: Affected customers: acme-inc, finapp, and a couple internal test clusters. Support ticket #12345 opened with initial symptoms (502/504).

alice.m: SSHing into nat-gw-12 to check conntrack/iptables. Give me 2 mins.

caro: We see gateway-proxy returning lots of "upstream reset" and connection timeouts in the runtime logs. Requests are queuing at proxy layer.

dmitri: I'll start packet captures on the proxy and NAT path to see if we have resets / RST floods.

alice.m: Conntrack metrics: nf_conntrack_count ~1.2M, nf_conntrack_max ~1.3M. Kernel logs: "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet". That explains new connection drops -> 504s/502s.

caro: That aligns with logs. If conntrack is full, NAT can't allocate ports -> upstream gets resets.

alice.m: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) increase nf_conntrack_max, 2) expand ephemeral port range, 3) roll back any recent SG changes that could block ephemeral ports, 4) failover to secondary NAT if needed.

dmitri: +1. Running quick commands now:```sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.hashsize=32768
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 61000"```

incident-bot: Runbook step: post initial customer-facing status update (ben_t). Next update in 15m.

ben_t: Posting: "We are investigating increased 5xx/timeouts for private VPC egress affecting some customers. Engineers are actively mitigating. Next update in 15 minutes."

alice.m: Applying sysctl changes on nat-gw-12...

alice.m: Output: "net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 2000000" applied. ip_local_port_range updated.

dmitri: tcpdump shows many FIN/RST from NAT to upstream and large volume of short-lived TCP connections in TIME_WAIT. Also lots of ephemeral port re-use.

eve-network: I see a recent security group change at 02:42 UTC that removed an outbound rule allowing ephemeral port ranges from nat-proxy-sg. Rolling back that change now to restore outbound ephemeral port allowance.

caro: If SG was blocking ephemeral ports outbound, that would cause NAT to attempt to reuse limited ports and fill conntrack. Good catch.

alice.m: After SG rollback and sysctl bump, error rate dropped to ~2% within 3 minutes. Most tenants back to normal. Still seeing residual 504s for long-lived streams; those may need retries from client side.

ben_t: Sending customer update: "Most traffic restored. We identified a misconfigured security group that blocked outbound ephemeral ports; engineers rolled back the change and increased system connection limits. We're monitoring and will follow up with a postmortem."

dmitri: Clearing stale conntrack entries for private ranges to speed recovery:```sudo conntrack -D -s 10.0.0.0/8 -p tcp```

alice.m: Handing off monitoring to eve-network (oncall-network-next) for overnight watch. Leaving commands, logs, and runbook pointers in this thread.

eve-network: Taking handoff. I'll keep alarms: conntrack_count > 1.5M OR error_rate > 3% -> page oncall. Also re-applying stricter auditing on SG change approval.

alice.m: thx team. Will open incident ticket and postmortem doc with timeline and mitigation steps. Closing active paging for now. :thumbsup:

ben_t: Customer update sent. I'll prepare a brief blameless note for postmortem and tag product/security if needed.

incident-bot: Incident resolved? status -> monitoring. Root cause summary: outbound ephemeral ports blocked by recent SG change + conntrack max not tuned for sudden connection spike. Mitigation: SG rollback, increased nf_conntrack_max, adjusted local port range, cleared stale conntrack entries. Postmortem in #incidents-docs.

alice.m: Adding follow-ups: - Add guardrail to block SG changes that remove ephemeral port ranges for NAT SGs - Add conntrack autoscaling alarm - Verify NAT high-availability failover path.

caro: Also add a runtime mitigation: graceful retry/backoff for long-lived streams and clearer 5xx classification to avoid cascading retries.

alice.m: Handoff complete. Last check-in 1834568205.
